action: Publica advises caution with unusual calls or messages (as reported by SRF) and posts updates at publica.ch/en/cyber-attack-software-supplier (per the admin.ch release). General advice: organisations should check which supplier test environments hold real personal data.
date_note: Date of Publica's announcement; the attack on its supplier was at the end of September 2026.
exec: A supplier's test environment held pension fund members' personal data, a reminder to control real data in non-production systems.
plain: The Swiss federal pension fund Publica says personal data of members may have leaked after its software supplier was hacked. Pensions are safe, and an outside audit has been ordered.

key_findings: Publica's software supplier PK Softech AG suffered a cyber attack at the end of September 2026.
Publica says it must assume personal data of current and former active members and pension recipients leaked from the test environment.
Publica's productive systems were not affected; it says pension assets and pensions are safe.
What data leaked and who is affected is not yet known; the audit ends by the end of January 2027, with a first report by the end of March 2027.

sources.name: admin.ch: Publica to commission external audit

summary: Swiss federal pension fund Publica said on 19 November it will commission an external audit after a late-September cyber attack on supplier PK Softech AG, and must assume members' personal data leaked from a test environment. SRF reported on 8 October that Publica named salary, AHV number and partner details among data probably taken. bluewin, citing SRF, reported an extortion attempt on 10 November; Publica and PK Softech told SRF they received no demand.
title: Swiss pension fund Publica to audit data handling after cyber attack on supplier PK Softech

validation.note: Official Swiss government press release read in full (primary). Follow-up 23 Nov: SRF (8 Oct) relays Publica's notice to insured persons on the data probably taken and says the Federal Prosecutor's Office is investigating; bluewin (10 Nov, English, citing SRF research) reports an extortion attempt the defence department is aware of, says federal authorities put those possibly affected at well over one hundred thousand current and former federal employees, and names a ransomware group it says the Federal Prosecutor's Office is investigating. No group named in the record: no prosecutor or government page making that attribution was read. letemps.ch follow-up answered 403.
